analysis.summary: Canada host Qatar at BC Place in Vancouver in a match that could decide Group B's early leader, with all four sides level on one point after Matchday 1 draws. Canada are heavy home co-host favourites backed by Jonathan David and Cyle Larin, while Qatar arrive in poor recent form (1W-1D-3L in last five) and rely on opportunism having salvaged a lucky own-goal equaliser against Switzerland. Alphonso Davies remains unavailable (hamstring), but Canada's squad depth still makes them clear favourites. A Canada win is the overwhelming expectation and the most likely outcome by a wide margin.
analysis.home_form: Canada drew 1-1 with Bosnia on June 12 (WC MD1) despite controlling play (xG 1.25 vs 0.98, 13-8 shots). Before the tournament they beat Uzbekistan 2-0 (Jun 1), drew Ireland 1-1 (Jun 5), drew Iceland 2-2 (Mar 28) and drew Tunisia 0-0 (Mar 31). Larin came off the bench to score; Jonathan David started and led the attack. Form trend: moderate — dominant but not clinical yet.
analysis.away_form: Qatar earned a creditable 1-1 draw vs Switzerland (WC MD1) but the equaliser was a 94th-minute own goal. In the five matches before the WC: lost 1-0 to Ireland (May 28), lost 0-3 to Tunisia (Dec 7), drew 1-1 with Syria (Dec 4), lost 0-1 to Palestine (Dec 1). Only one win (unconfirmed) in the last 5 competitive fixtures. Qatar ranked 55th globally; conceded 1.56 goals per game in Asian qualifying.
analysis.h2h: Only one prior meeting: September 23, 2022 friendly in Vienna. Canada won 2-0, goals from Cyle Larin and Jonathan David — the same two attackers in the squad now.
injuries_news: Alphonso Davies (Canada) — right hamstring strain sustained May 6 vs Bayern Munich, not expected to start; targeting Match 3 vs Switzerland.
Marcelo Flores (Canada) — major knee injury, replaced by Jayden Nelson in squad.
Moise Bombito (Canada) — recovering from serious leg injury, availability unconfirmed.
No significant injury concerns reported for Qatar squad.
key_factors: Canada playing at home in Vancouver with partisan crowd; BC Place expected to be near-capacity.
Alphonso Davies absence means Richie Laryea starts at left-back, slightly weakening Canada's best attacking threat down that flank.
Jonathan David (8 goals, 5 assists for Juventus this season) and Cyle Larin (8 goals for Southampton) form a potent strike partnership.
Qatar's defensive frailty: conceded 1.56 goals/game in Asian qualifying and relied on a last-minute own goal vs Switzerland — limited clean-sheet ability.
Qatar showed resilience in holding Switzerland but have below-par form in recent months (3 losses from 4 pre-WC matches).
A Canada win moves them top of Group B; a draw keeps all four teams level going into the final matchday — Canada's motivation is high.
Both sides need points: a Canada win puts them in a commanding position; Qatar need at minimum a draw to stay in contention.
